html:
The Boyana Church is a small medieval Orthodox church on the edge of Sofia, the capital of Bulgaria, famous for frescoes painted in 1259. Its oldest part dates from the late 10th or early 11th century. A second part was added in the 13th century, under the Second Bulgarian Empire, by the local lord Kaloyan, a relative of the royal family.

The 1259 paintings, by an unknown master, cover the walls with some 240 figures in 89 scenes. What makes them famous is their life. The faces are individual and full of feeling, and the portraits of the donor Kaloyan and his wife Desislava, and of Tsar Konstantin Tikh and Tsaritsa Irina, look like real people. Many scholars see them as a high point of medieval art in Eastern Europe, painted a generation before Giotto moved Italian painting in a similar direction.

The church was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1979.
